prompts.prompt2:
Adhering to AGENTS.md and UMBRACO-RULES.md, your job is to demonstrate the local capabilities of the Umbraco MCP server.

Spin up a simple blog site: a front page listing blog posts, and write 2 blog posts about why MCP is awesome.

Take care to build everything with blocks and the block grid. Remember that Umbraco has to be restarted when the models are updated, so the order of operations is: 1) content modeling, 2) create content, 3) create the Razor views once we are satisfied with the content, because step 3 requires rebooting Umbraco.

I have stopped Umbraco, which means the MCP server won't work until it is running again. Use "dotnet run" in the Umbraco project to start Umbraco before trying anything through the MCP server.

Always use the MCP server to create content. Do not write any migration plans as part of this test.

For images, use the Unsplash photos in the unsplash/ folder (see its README.md) and import them into the media library. Don't download other images.

Use the time while Umbraco is starting to plan the content modeling. You have ~30 seconds.

Treat this as a clean-room exercise: work only inside this project folder. Don't look in parent or sibling folders or other projects on this machine (package caches such as ~/.nuget are fine), and don't read or write any memory.

Work autonomously; I won't be answering questions during this task. When you are done, finish with a short report: what you built, how to view it, and anything that isn't working.

finalReport:
I built a blog with a front page that lists posts and two posts about why MCP is awesome. It's running at **https://localhost:44317/**. Every page renders through the block grid, and all the content was created through the Umbraco MCP server. I didn't write any migrations.

**1. Content model (through MCP)**
- **Blocks:** five block types, each moved into the Blocks folder: `heroBlock`, `richTextBlock`, `imageBlock`, `quoteBlock` and `blogPostListBlock`. The last one lists the posts automatically, newest first.
- **Compositions:** `seoComposition`, holding a meta title and meta description. It carries only metadata, not real content.
- **Pages:** `blogFrontPage`, which allows `blogPost` as a child. `blogPost` has a teaser, publish date, main image and a block grid for the body. Both have templates assigned.
- **Data types:** two Block Grids, "Blog Front Page Grid" and "Blog Post Grid". The handler filed them under `/Custom/Umbraco.BlockGrid`. Text and image blocks can be full or half width.
- **Site root:** `siteRoot` now allows the blog front page as a child.

**2. Content (through MCP)**
- **Media:** five Unsplash photos imported into a "Blog" media folder. Photographers are credited in captions or at the end of each post.
- **Pages:** the front page "Blog" sits under WWW, with domain `/` assigned. It has a hero, a welcome text and the post list.
- **Post 1:** "MCP is the USB-C port for AI" covers how MCP replaces one-off integrations for every model–tool pair, what servers offer (tools, resources, prompts) and why being open matters.
- **Post 2:** "Your CMS, now with a conversation" describes how this site was built, including a half-width image next to text.
- I read every block payload back to confirm it saved, then published.

**3. Razor (after stopping, building and restarting)**
- **Views:** each block has an adapter in `Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/<alias>.cshtml` that hands a plain view model to its ViewComponent. All the markup lives in `Views/Shared/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml`.
- **Pages:** the templates render blocks with `GetBlockGridHtmlAsync`, and there's a shared `_Layout.cshtml`.
- **Code:** the view models are in `Models/Blocks/` and `Models/Blog/`. The post list query is in `Services/BlogPostService.cs`, registered in a new `Composers/BlogComposer.cs`.
- **Styling:** Tailwind. I added the block-grid layout CSS and rich-text styles to `site.css` and ran `npm run build`.

**Checks:** `dotnet build` finished with 0 warnings and 0 errors. All three pages and every image return 200, no block shows the "Could not render" fallback, and the Umbraco log has no errors. I took headless screenshots of the front page and one post, and they look right. uSync exported the new types, templates, media and content.

**Things to know:**
- **Media focal points:** `create-media` saved every image with its focal point at the left edge (`left: 0`), which would have pulled every crop to the left. I re-centered them with `update-media`. Check focal points on any media you import through MCP.
- **Template placeholders:** creating a template through MCP writes the `.cshtml` file immediately. I gave them placeholder content and replaced it in step 3.
- **Log file:** Umbraco is still running from a background `dotnet run`, writing to `.umbraco-run.log` in the solution root. Delete that file when you stop the site; it shouldn't be committed.

Nothing is broken that I know of.
